feed.title: Combined summary - DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol

entry.title: Combined summary - DropKick ⚽️ - A minimal commit/reveal PQ rescue protocol
entry.summary: DropKick is a newly introduced commit/reveal protocol designed specifically to assist Bitcoin users, who are delayed in transferring their assets into Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) enabled wallets by the designated Q-Day. It operates by recording a hidden commitment on the blockchain, which can be later revealed through an SPV-style proof to enable the spending of legacy coins in a new PQ-secure wallet. This system leverages the blockchain's trustless timestamping to prove the early knowledge of a secret witness, thus protecting it against potential threats from quantum computers. The core mechanism of DropKick involves embedding the commitment `H(H(w, Q), Q)` within a block using methods like OP_RETURN or a taproot tweak, where `Q` denotes a post-quantum public key and `w` is a witness to a one-way function `f`. At the time of transaction, this witness along with a signature from `Q` facilitates coin spending. The verifier is responsible for confirming the validity and age of the commitment opening, verifying the calculation `s = f(x)`, and validating the PQ-signature from `Q`. DropKick is distinct in its compatibility across various one-way functions and does not necessitate the confiscation of any coins, applying specifically to UTXOs with decidable knowledge asymmetries. Its design minimizes impact on the blockchain until the reveal phase, where the commitment opening proofs consume minimal space and resources. Furthermore, it allows users to operate without personal PQ-safe UTXOs by utilizing third-party aggregators who manage these commitments collectively. Comparatively, DropKick offers a simpler implementation than Tadge Dryja’s Lifeboat/Lifejacket protocols, albeit with potentially lower security due to its relaxed commitment ordering requirement. Unlike Lifeboat, which requires validators to index all commitments chronologically, DropKick uses merkle trees to embed commitments indirectly through blocks, eliminating the need for a centralized index database and reducing on-chain visibility. This reduces centralization and broadens the rescue scenarios for users, though it necessitates a longer delay between the commit and reveal phases based on the UTXO value at stake. Despite these trade-offs, DropKick provides a flexible and efficient solution aimed at improving user experience in post-quantum cryptocurrency transactions. For more comprehensive details on the proving and verifying steps in the DropKick protocol, please visit [conduition.io/bitcoin/dropkick](https://conduition.io/bitcoin/dropkick). To address a common misconception, it's important to note that DropKick's functionality does depend on the existence of a valid PQC solution and pre-existing PQC UTXOs available in the system. Thus, it serves as a solution specifically for individual Bitcoin users rather than the Bitcoin system as a whole, which must have a deployed and functioning PQC framework beforehand for DropKick to be operational.
